newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker rates flat, good enquiry in Med.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker rates flat, good enquiry in Med.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were little changed in quiet trade in most sectors on Monday, brokers said.
They said 80,000 tonne vessels in the Mediterranean were seeing good enquiry with up to five offers per cargo but rates seemed set to remain steady at around W130.
"There are a fair number of vessels being offered but I don't see the market moving very much. It looks like a slow start to the week," one broker said.
Million-barrel (130,000 tonne) Med cargoes were dormant. Middle East rates were flat, with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to the west and to Singapore remaining at W50.
To Japan they were around W65.
West Africa/U.S. VLCCs also held steady at W67.5, while million-barrel vessels remained at about W90/92.5, with cargoes from the North Sea to the U.S. at similar rates.
Brokers said the inter-U.K./Cont crude sector showed little sign of movement too, with 80,000 tonners at around W90/95.
But inter-U.K./Cont fuel oil was slightly weaker at W200/205 in a sluggish market, with Baltic cargoes at a 10-point winter premium due to ice.
The U.S. sector was no livelier, with 70,000 tonne Caribs/upcoast crude cargoes slipping to W132.5/135 from W140.
50,000 tonne fuel oil vessels were steady at W170/175.
U.S. fuel oil has slipped some 10 points in recent weeks, having averaged W185.64 in the period Jan 7-Feb 6, according to the Reuters Tanker Industry Index.
